title: Rate Limiting Middleware
description: Build a rate-limiting middleware for Express that tracks requests per IP and blocks excessive traffic with configurable limits.

steps.title: Basic API endpoint
steps.description: Create a GET /api endpoint that returns a success response. This will be the endpoint we protect with rate limiting.
hints: Use app.get('/api', handler) to define the route
Return JSON with a message and timestamp

steps.title: Rate limit exceeded
steps.description: Simulate rate limiting by making 5+ rapid requests. After the limit is exceeded, the server should return 429 Too Many Requests.
hints: Track request counts per IP address in an in-memory object
Define a limit (e.g., 5 requests) and a window (e.g., 10 seconds)
If the count exceeds the limit, return 429 with { error: 'Too many requests' }

steps.title: Refactor rate limiter middleware
steps.description: Refactor the rate limiting logic into a reusable `rateLimiter` middleware function that accepts options like limit and window duration.
hints: Create a function: rateLimiter({ windowMs, max }) => (req, res, next) => { ... }
Clean up old entries periodically to prevent memory leaks
Set the rate limit info on the response headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)

steps.title: Different limits per route
steps.description: Configure different rate limits for different routes. For example, /api/expensive has a lower limit (2 req/10s) while /api/cheap has a higher limit (10 req/10s).
hints: Create multiple rateLimiter instances with different options
Apply specific rate limiters to specific routes via app.use('/api/expensive', ...)
Test that the expensive route hits 429 faster than the cheap route
